sections.section_title: Pathophysiology of HIT and the Spectrum of Autoimmune HIT (aHIT)
sections.description: This section establishes the foundational knowledge required to understand the case, contrasting the mechanism of classic Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT) with the more severe, heparin-independent variant, autoimmune HIT (aHIT).
subtopics: Mechanism of classic HIT: PF4-heparin immune complexes and Fc receptor clustering
Clinical characteristics of HIT: Thrombocytopenia vs. hypercoagulability
Introduction to autoimmune HIT (aHIT): Definition and heparin-independent platelet activation
Clinical implications of aHIT: Severity of thrombocytopenia and risk of thrombosis
Comparison of risk factors: Cardiac surgery and cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) as primary triggers

sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Diagnostic Reasoning in the Postoperative Period
sections.description: This section walks through the patient's clinical course, focusing on the challenge of distinguishing HIT from other causes of rapid postoperative thrombocytopenia.
subtopics: The surgical context: Preoperative catheterization and cardiopulmonary bypass
Timeline analysis: The significance of early platelet decline (before POD 5)
Differential diagnosis of postoperative thrombocytopenia: Infection, TTP, and drug-induced causes
Identifying the 'trigger': The role of preoperative heparin exposure in early-onset HIT
Neurological complications: Identifying stroke as a manifestation of HIT-associated hypercoagulability

sections.section_title: Advanced Laboratory Interpretation: The Serotonin Release Assay (SRA)
sections.description: This section explains the specific diagnostic workup of this case, focusing on the interpretation of atypical and 'indeterminate' laboratory results that confirmed aHIT.
subtopics: Screening vs. Confirmatory testing: PF4/polyanion ELISA and the SRA
Interpreting 'Indeterminate' SRA results: Analyzing serotonin release at 0, 0.1, and 0.3 U/mL heparin
Heparin-independent activation: Identifying the hallmark of aHIT in the SRA
Fc receptor blockade: Explaining the atypical partial inhibition by the IV.3 monoclonal antibody
Evolution of serology: How antibody profiles can change during the recovery phase

sections.section_title: Management Strategies for Severe and Refractory HIT
sections.description: This section details the clinical decision-making process regarding the choice of anticoagulants and adjunctive therapies for a patient with high-risk aHIT.
subtopics: Initial management: Selecting direct thrombin inhibitors (argatroban) over fondaparinux
The role of high-dose intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) in aHIT
Monitoring treatment efficacy: Using fibrinogen levels, d-dimer, and peripheral blood films
Managing refractory hypercoagulability: Indications for switching to fondaparinux
Anticoagulation transition: Safety considerations for resuming oral anticoagulation (apixaban)

sections.description: This section synthesizes the unique aspects of the case to provide high-yield takeaways for clinical practice, focusing on early detection and recognizing severe phenotypes.
subtopics: Recognizing early-onset HIT: The importance of reviewing preoperative heparin exposure
Identifying 'red flags' for aHIT: Profound thrombocytopenia and consumptive coagulopathy (schistocytes)
The danger of 'indeterminate' results: Avoiding missed diagnoses in complex serological profiles
Long-term outcomes and the waning of aHIT antibodies
Summary of the clinical logic: From surgical history to specialized immunology
